messages.author: cd08a634ebdbdfa2
messages.subject: SparkR Streaming
parts:
Hi all,

It was great to see SparkR treated as first class citizen during Spark Summit East talks.
I wanted to check if there is any plans of supporting Spark's streaming with R? I see there is jira ticket open with no updates.

My requirement is to use a model developed in R on a stream of incoming input. I don't really need to have streaming context accessed in R. Its more like a Storm Bolt written in R.
I want to avoid starting R process for each block. Do you have any thoughts on having a "R process" per worker that can take input, apply a function and return output? Something like Rserve may be??

Thanks,
Srikanth

messages.author: f4108b5f63668d70
messages.subject: Re: SparkR Streaming
parts:
I'm not an expert in Spark streaming and Davies (cc'd) can probably throw some light on how one can use something like a Storm Bolt in Spark streaming.

Regarding the second point of starting R processes each time, we already use a long running R daemon on each machine and because of that the fork overhead should be pretty low for each worker. We also have PR open to add profiling for this [1], so we can measure how much overhead we have.

Thanks
Shivaram

[1] https://github.com/amplab-extras/SparkR-pkg/pull/208

messages.author: cd08a634ebdbdfa2
messages.subject: Re: SparkR Streaming
parts:
Thanks Shivaram for the clarification. I somehow thought that in SparkR the Scala worker was internally launching a new R process during each stage. Did that change recently or was that the behavior from beginning?

Davies,
Thanks for listing out priority for SparkR. That really helps(although I'd have loved to see streaming up the list!!)
I'm not sure if forking R process would take just a few ms. Counting the time it would take to fork, setup environment, source one or two R files and load couple of libraries.

Thanks,
Srikanth


On Fri, Mar 20, 2015 at 3:08 PM, Davies Liu <dav...@databricks.com> wrote:
I think SparkR is still in early stage, we are focus on API for Spark
Core and SQL, which should
be most important ones for data scientists. MLlib may come before streaming.

The model in Spark Streaming is much different than Storm, microbatch
VS pipeline. The overhead of schedule a batch in Spark Stream is about
100ms, which is much higher than Storm, then forking a R process for
each batch is acceptable (which contribute a few of ms).

We re-use the workers in PySpark, the most benefits is that we could
re-used the broadcasted objects, but the implementation is
complicated, introduced several bugs. We should avoid that in SparkR
(at least in near future).

Thanks,
